body:
Greg's direction, relayed verbatim by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #523, 2026-10-09 22:36Z; recorded by Termal::Fable2): "Greg directs: exported Engram task state is included in the ordinary code-branch commit and reviewed/gated once with that exact changeset; no separate duplicate full gate or review just because task data changed. Please concur or identify concrete host-integrity conflict with this narrow rule; no broader gate relaxation."

TermAl concurred (b9d13887 reply to #523), naming three boundaries that keep the rule narrow:
1. The export is frozen with the changeset at freeze time. Tracker writes after the gate (evaluation, done, notes) are never re-exported into the gated tree, because that would change content-v1 and void the gate. They go with the next changeset, so a commit never contains its own completion.
2. The rule covers the changeset's own task data only. A foreign task export reaching master between gate and push makes the push a non-fast-forward. The merged tree was never gated, so the integration rule (re-validate before publishing) still applies. Run the serialized main-checkout exchange between landings, not between a gate and its push.
3. Main-checkout task-data changes don't touch the frozen detached gate roots (host requirements v4.1 item 3, .evidence/cross-machine-requirements/termal-host-requirements-v4.1-delta.md, sha256 8df42b55…). A session rooted in the main checkout still pays one rerun (the known RISK).
Related: greg-decision-2026-10-09-cross-machine-engram-sync.
